neighbours.label: systems-theory vocabulary: cybernetics, self-organization, complex systems, systems thinking
fire: Norbert Wiener founded cybernetics as the study of control and feedback.
Ant colonies are a classic example of self-organization without a leader.
The course introduces complex systems, emergence and nonlinear dynamics.
In systems thinking, the behavior of the whole arises from feedback between its parts.
Second-order cybernetics treats the observer as part of the system.
Ecologists study the complexity of food webs as adaptive systems.
The theory of self-organizing systems explains how order emerges from noise.
Bateson brought ideas from cybernetics into anthropology and psychiatry.
quiet: Norbert Wiener was a child prodigy who studied mathematics at Harvard.
Ant colonies are a classic example of insects that live underground.
The course introduces organic chemistry, reaction rates and titration.
In classical music, the melody is often carried by the first violins.
Medieval historians treat the chronicler as an unreliable witness.
Ecologists study the diet of wolves in the northern forests.
The theory of plate tectonics explains how mountains rise from the sea floor.
Bateson brought ideas from biology into his work on island cultures.

notes: Card: 'net' in cybernetics x2 (also Russian кибернетика), 'organization' in self-organization x3, ' systems' x4, ' complexity'. Logit promotes dynamics, processes, models. Near misses keep academic science prose about other subjects.
